title: Best Liquor Store POS System: 7 Leading Solutions
summary: Explore our list of 7 leading liquor store POS systems and what they offer. Review ecommerce, inventory, and other features to pick the best fit for your shop.
body_text: Your POS system is there to make running your liquor store easier, and picking the right one for your business is one of the most important long-term decisions you’ll make. If you make the right decision, you’ll save hours of manual data entry, stop reconciling delivery-app sales by hand, and make inventory errors a thing of the past. How Important Is It to Choose a POS System Designed for Liquor Stores? Some store owners still treat their POS systems as nothing more than cash registers that ring up sales and take payments, missing out on features that can dramatically improve their business outcomes. A liquor-specific POS is built around the reality of running a liquor store, and it addresses the most critical pain points that you and your staff face every day. The best liquor store POS systems can help you turn daily chaos into a simple, repeatable flow: It can help you with orders and invoices, making a once tedious manual task a five-minute chore Ensure that every SKU is named, priced, and paired with the right image and product details, so that it's easy for your customers to find the products they want Never miss a sale with your inventory and pricing in sync across in-store, online, and delivery apps Elevate your customer service with one unified profile for each customer, where you can see their purchase history across all of your channels Drive repeat purchases with a loyalty programs that encourage your customers to make all of their beverage purchases with you Boost eCommerce sales with SEO strategies that are tailor-made for your product catalog Integrate with delivery apps and industry marketplaces to make your product catalog available everywhere your customers shop Handle complex products, like beers, RTDs, changing wine vintages, kegs, and lottery tickets, without compromising inventory or pricing accuracy When tailored to the liquor industry’s unique challenges, your POS becomes the central operating system of your shop, saves hours of manual work, keeps inventory in sync across all channels, and gives you the tools to grow your business. That's why today you can choose between multiple POS systems built specifically to address the challenges of managing liquor stores. We will now present the top 7 liquor store POS systems, featuring industry-leading solutions. #1 Santé POS Santé is a complete, industry-specific POS that consolidates eCommerce, marketing, and back office tools into a single, easy-to-use platform. It is the core operating system of your business that does much more than process transactions and track inventory. Santé saves you 15+ hours every week with AI that simplifies annoying back office tasks so that you can focus on servicing your customers. You can devote this time to selling with Santé’s eCommerce platform and marketing suite that puts your store in front of customers where they are: online, on their mobile device. Highlights AI Invoice Receiving that cuts manual data entry and enables you to receive invoices in seconds Custom eCommerce websites that come equipped with product images, descriptions, details and ratings Automated SEO strategies that elevate your website’s page ranking on search engines and AI chat platforms Marketing tools that trigger email and SMS campaigns based your customer’s shopping history Real-time integrations with delivery platforms like DoorDash, Instacart, GrubHub and UberEats so that you can accept these orders directly in Santé Pack and case management so that you can break beers and RTDs down into multiple variations from one SKU Jurisdiction-level tax rules that support state, country, city and category taxes - both in-store and online Bottle deposits and keg deposits so that are automatically applied at the register with easy payouts on returns when customers bring these containers back to you store Flexible loyalty program that encourages your customers to make beverage purchases exclusively with your store Age verification prompts and ID checks at checkout that gives you the ability to create customer profiles directly from the ID scan Quickbooks Desktop and Online integration that includes daily Journal Entries and real-time feeds for Bills and Vendor Credits With features designed for off-premise retail, Santé stands out as the best POS system for liquor stores. With one unified system that is built to grow your business, you’ll experience more sales - both in-store and online - and you’ll save hours on back office work that holds you back. #2 Square Square is a general-purpose POS system that works well for smaller liquor stores that want quick setup, reliable card processing, and an easy way to sell both in-store and online. It combines checkout, basic inventory, and Square Online into a single package, allowing you to get started quickly and maintain simple operations with a lean team. Highlights Built-in payments with straightforward setup and no separate merchant account. Square Online for click-and-collect, local delivery options, and curbside pickup. Barcode scanning, basic inventory counts, and low-stock alerts. Customer profiles, email receipts, and an optional loyalty add-on to encourage repeat visits. Team management, permissions, and time tracking to keep shifts organized. Integrations for accounting, marketing, and delivery couriers via the Square app marketplace. Hardware options, from handheld readers to countertop stations, you can scale as you grow. If you’re looking for a low-friction start, Square reduces the learning curve and keeps daily tasks manageable. You get a clean checkout, a simple way to list products online, and fewer moving parts to worry about. #3 Bottle POS Bottle POS is purpose-built for alcohol retail. It covers age verification, case-break and pack pricing, deposits/fees, and mix-and-match rules while keeping on-hand counts accurate. It links the counter, purchasing, and online orders, so changes are continually updated across all platforms. Highlights ID scanning and age prompts at checkout (1D/2D barcode support). Case-break logic, mix-and-match, quantity breaks, and deposits/CRV handling. Purchase orders, vendor catalogs, and invoice receiving with cost/margin updates. eCommerce module with shared catalog, curbside, and delivery workflows. Promotions and loyalty with coupon rules and customer profiles. QuickBooks sync and accounting exports with tax mapping for alcohol categories. Barcode generation, label/shelf-tag printing, and stock adjustments. With Bottle POS, you make fewer pricing and inventory corrections, complete ID checks faster, and process cleaner reorders from accurate on-hand data. Staff members ring singles, packs, and cases correctly, and the website accurately reflects real-time stock, which reduces out-of-stocks and margin slippage. ‍ #4 Atlantic Systems (SPIRITS POS) SPIRITS is a liquor-specific POS built by Atlantic Systems, focused on compliance, inventory accuracy, and back-office control. It covers front-end checkout with age verification and ties into purchasing, pricing, and reporting for single or multi-store setups. Atlantic Systems brings 40 years of liquor industry expertise with highly automated inventory management, sophisticated analytics, and reliable support from people who understand liquor retail. Highlights Age verification prompts and ID checks at checkout. Inventory control with case/mix-and-match pricing and vintage handling. Purchase orders, vendor files, and invoice receiving with cost updates. eCommerce/catalog capabilities with inventory sync. Sales/tax reports and accounting exports, including QuickBooks. Multi-store transfers and centralized reporting. Spirits GO mobile app for real-time sales and inventory views. If you want proven reliability, excellent support, and don't need modern cloud features or mobile access, Atlantic Systems delivers time-tested stability. You get dependable checkout, precise inventory and pricing controls, detailed reports, and responsive, liquor-specific support. However, it operates as an on-premise system without cloud or mobile access, which means no remote dashboards, limited third-party integrations, and updates/backups handled on your own server. #5 Korona POS KORONA is a cloud-based retail POS that many liquor stores use for age checks, inventory control, and multi-location management. It’s managed through the KORONA Studio back office, so you can monitor sales, stock, and pricing from anywhere. Highlights Age prompts/ID verification at checkout. Cloud back office (KORONA Studio) with remote reporting and controls. Inventory with automated reordering, stock alerts, and movement/ABC analysis. Purchase orders, vendor files, and invoice receiving with cost updates. eCommerce integration (native WooCommerce; third-party connectors available). Promotions, discounts, gift cards, and loyalty/CRM options. Supports multiple processors (choose your merchant services); multi-store and centralized reporting. You get remote access to sales and inventory, consistent pricing across locations, and fewer stock surprises thanks to automated reorders and alerts. If you run WooCommerce (or plan to), it syncs catalog and counts from the POS, reducing double entry while keeping online and in-store inventory aligned. #6 Lightspeed Retail Lightspeed Retail is a cloud POS used by many retailers, including liquor stores that want strong inventory tools, multi-store controls, and a polished eCommerce stack. With add-ons like Hyperspace Age Verification and built-in online options, it covers in-store checkout, catalog sync, and remote back-office management. Highlights Age verification via the Hyperspace app (license scanning; web and tablet support). Cloud back office with remote reporting and controls. Inventory with purchase orders, cost updates, barcode/label printing, and low-stock tools. eCommerce options: Lightspeed eCom (E-Series) with product/stock sync; WooCommerce connectors available. Multi-store management and centralized data across outlets/channels. Integration marketplace and third-party apps (marketing, accounting, shipping). 24/7 support and a supported hardware ecosystem Lightspeed retail excels at sophisticated e-commerce, offering native selling across TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, Amazon, and eBay, along with advanced features such as wine club management and event booking. However, it requires the use of their processors at higher rates with no opportunity for negotiation. It's also built for general retail rather than liquor-specific needs, and lacks automated case breaking, bottle deposit handling, and excise tax management, while recent stability issues and declining support quality add operational challenges . #7 mPower Beverage POS mPower is a liquor-specific POS with deep inventory control, suggested ordering, and multi-store management. It’s primarily on-premise with remote access options and integrates with websites so online stock and pricing reflect what’s in the store. Highlights Age verification with 2D driver’s license scanning at checkout. Need-to-order reports using sales velocity, par counts, and case deals. Purchase orders, vendor files, and invoice receiving with cost updates. Multi-store sync for pricing, transfers, and centralized reporting. eCommerce/website integrations with shared catalog and inventory levels. QuickBooks export/integration for accounting handoff. Handheld/line-busting and remote access for counts and receiving. With mature liquor workflows and broad integration options, mPower fits retailers who want granular pricing and reporting without switching their whole web stack. The tradeoff is an older, Windows-first feel compared to newer cloud suites, but the operational depth and accounting ties are strong for brick-and-mortar-led stores. Get The Best Liquor Store POS System For Your Store Choosing from the selection of top liquor store POS systems should feel practical and reassuring, as you are getting a POS system designed to tackle the unique challenges of the liquor industry. The right platform streamlines tasks like invoicing, labeling, and reordering into quick actions, keeps every channel in sync, and makes it clear what to stock and when. Your team learns it quickly, loyalty and marketing run in one place, and repeat sales start to climb. If you want to see how much easier it can be to run a liquor store with a POS tailored to how your store works, try Santé POS and judge it by what your next month of operations looks like.

title: Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. Announces Third Quarter 2025 Results

body_text: Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. Announces Third Quarter 2025 Results November 04, 2025 7:15 am EST Download as PDF Related Documents Presentation PDF 10-Q Filing HTML PDF XBRL ZIP Reports Third Quarter Net Investment Income of $0.43 per Share Declares Fourth Quarter Regular Distribution of $0.45 per Share NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. (NYSE: NCDL) (“NCDL” or the “Company”), a business development company externally managed by its investment adviser, Churchill DLC Advisor LLC (the “Adviser”), and by its sub-adviser, Churchill Asset Management LLC (“Churchill”), today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Financial Highlights for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2025 Net investment income of $0.43 per share Net realized and unrealized loss on investments of $(0.05) per share Net increase in net assets resulting from operations of $0.38 per share Net asset value ("NAV") per share of $17.85, compared to $17.92 per share as of June 30, 2025 Paid third quarter regular distribution of $0.45 per share on October 28, 2025, which represents a 10.0% total annualized distribution yield based on the third quarter NAV per share Declared fourth quarter regular distribution of $0.45 per share “We are pleased with our financial results and the continued strong performance of our portfolio during the third quarter,” said Ken Kencel, President and Chief Executive Officer of NCDL and Churchill. “We are encouraged by the positive momentum and pickup in transaction activity, which we believe will continue into next year. As we look ahead to 2026, NCDL remains well-positioned with respect to our experienced investment team, high-quality diversified portfolio and strong capital structure.” “NCDL continues to operate from a position of strength, in our view, with ample liquidity and no near-term debt maturities,” said Shai Vichness, Chief Financial Officer of NCDL and Churchill. “Looking ahead, we remain focused on continuing to invest in high quality assets, optimizing our capital structure, and delivering attractive risk-adjusted returns for our shareholders.” Distribution Declaration The Company’s Board of Directors (the "Board") has declared a fourth quarter 2025 regular distribution of $0.45 per share payable on January 27, 2026 to shareholders of record as of December 31, 2025. PORTFOLIO COMPOSITION As of September 30, 2025, the fair value of the Company's portfolio investments was $2.0 billion across 213 portfolio companies in 26 industries compared to $2.0 billion as of June 30, 2025 across 207 portfolio companies in 26 industries. As of September 30, 2025, the Company’s portfolio based on fair value consisted of approximately 89.8% first-lien debt investments, 8.1% subordinated debt investments, and 2.1% equity investments. As of June 30, 2025, the Company’s portfolio based on fair value consisted of 90.0% first-lien debt investments, 8.0% subordinated debt investments, and 2.0% equity investments. As of September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2025, the weighted average Internal Risk Rating of the portfolio at fair value was 4.2 and 4.1 (4.0 being the initial rating assigned at origination), respectively. As of September 30, 2025, there were investments in three portfolio companies on non-accrual status representing 0.4% of total investments at fair value (or 0.9% of total investments at cost). As of June 30, 2025, there were investments in one portfolio company on non-accrual status representing 0.2% of total investments at fair value (or 0.4% of total investments at cost). PORTFOLIO AND INVESTMENT ACTIVITY For the three months ended September 30, 2025, the Company funded $36.3 million of portfolio investments and received $61.3 million of proceeds from principal repayments and sales, compared to $81.1 million and $162.2 million, respectively, for the three months ended June 30, 2025. RESULTS OF OPERATIONS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2025 Investment Income Investment income for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was $51.1 million compared to $60.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2024. As of September 30, 2025 and September 30, 2024, the size of the Company's portfolio was $2.0 billion and $2.1 billion, at cost, respectively. As of September 30, 2025, the weighted average yield of debt and income producing investments decreased to 9.92% from 10.86% as of September 30, 2024, at cost, primarily due to overall tightening of spreads in newly originated investments and the decline in base interest rates. Net Expenses Net expenses increased to $29.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 from $28.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2024, primarily due to an increase in management fees and income-based incentive fees, offset by a decrease in interest and debt financing expenses. The increase in management fees was primarily attributable to the increase in the management fee base rate from 0.75% to 1.00%, effective March 31, 2025, pursuant to the terms of the Advisory Agreement. Additionally, effective March 31, 2025, the Adviser's waiver of incentive fees on income and on capital gains expired pursuant to the terms of the Advisory Agreement. For the three months ended September 30, 2025, income-based incentive fees were $3.3 million. Interest and debt financing expenses decreased primarily due to lower average daily borrowings and a lower average annual interest rate. Net Realized Gain (Loss) and Net Change in Unrealized Gain (Loss) on Investments For the three months ended September 30, 2025, the Company recorded a net realized gain on investments of $1.5 million compared to a net realized gain of $1.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2024. The net realized gain for the three months ended September 30, 2025 was primarily driven by a realization of an equity investment during the period. The Company recorded a net change in unrealized loss of $(4.2) million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, which resulted primarily from decreases in fair value of certain underperforming portfolio investments. Financial Condition, Liquidity and Capital Resources As of September 30, 2025, the Company had $46.3 million in cash and cash equivalents and $1.1 billion in total aggregate principal amount of debt outstanding. Subject to borrowing base and other conditions, the Company had approximately $269.5 million available for additional borrowings under its revolving credit facility as of September 30, 2025. At September 30, 2025, the Company's debt to equity ratio was 1.25x (1.20x net debt to equity ratio) compared to 1.26x (1.21x net to debt equity ratio) at June 30, 2025. All interested parties may participate in the conference call by dialing (866) 605-1826 approximately 10-15 minutes prior to the call; international callers should dial +1 (215) 268-9877. Participants should reference Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. when prompted. A live webcast of the conference call will also be available on the Events section of the Company's website at https://www.ncdl.com/news/events . A replay will be available under the same link following the conclusion of the conference call. About Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. Nuveen Churchill Direct Lending Corp. (“NCDL”) is a specialty finance company focused primarily on investing in senior secured loans to private equity-owned U.S. middle market companies. NCDL has elected to be regulated as a business development company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended. Both the investment adviser and sub-adviser are affiliates and subsidiaries of Nuveen, LLC (“Nuveen”), the investment management division of Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America (“TIAA”) and one of the largest asset managers globally. Churchill is a leading capital provider for private equity-backed middle market companies and operates as the exclusive U.S. middle market direct lending and private capital business of Nuveen and TIAA. body_text: View All News Kinetik Reports Third Quarter 2025 Financial and Operating Results and Revises 2025 Financial Guidance November 5, 2025 HOUSTON & MIDLAND, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Kinetik Holdings Inc. (NYSE: KNTK) (“ Kinetik ” or the “ Company ”) today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2025. Kinetik reported net income including noncontrolling interest of $15.5 million and $109.2 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Kinetik generated Adjusted EBITDA1 of $242.6 million and $735.6 million, Distributable Cash Flow1 of $158.5 million and $468.8 million, and Free Cash Flow1 of $50.9 million and $179.2 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. Highlights Closed divestiture of 27.5% non-operated equity interest in EPIC Crude Holdings, LP (“ EPIC Crude ”) Achieved full commercial in-service at the Kings Landing Complex (“ Kings Landing ”) in late September 2025 Revising 2025 Adjusted EBITDA 1 Guidance range to $965 million to $1.005 billion as outlined in the Outlook & Guidance section Refining 2025 Capital Guidance range to $485 million to $515 million, including growth and maintenance Reached final investment decision (“ FID ”) on the acid gas injection (“ AGI ”) project at Kings Landing Finalized agreement for a residue natural gas pipeline connection for a new 1,350 MW gas-fired power generation facility owned by Competitive Power Ventures, Inc. (“ CPV ”) Executed new five-year liquefied natural gas (“ LNG ”) pricing agreement with INEOS Energy (“ INEOS ”) for a total of 0.5 million tonnes per annum (“ MTPA ”) at Port Arthur LNG Secured additional natural gas transport capacity to the U.S. Gulf Coast to meet growing customer demand CEO Commentary “Kinetik achieved a significant milestone in the third quarter of 2025 with the full commercial in-service of Kings Landing, adding critical processing capacity in New Mexico,” said Jamie Welch, Kinetik’s President & Chief Executive Officer. “The additional processing capacity is a significant step for our Delaware North customers, returning new volumes behind our system that had been curtailed for up to two years while also enabling resumption of development plans and new activity across the system. And today, we announced FID on the AGI project at Kings Landing, further positioning Kinetik to capture the significant sour gas opportunity in the Northern Delaware.” “The Permian continues to stand out - it remains one of the lowest cost sources of incremental hydrocarbons globally, and its producers continue to extract efficiency gains as they do more with less. That said, the Permian is not fully insulated from the current commodity headwinds. Delaware Basin rig count is down nearly 20% since the start of the year, and the Permian experienced substantial production shut-ins as Waha natural gas prices were negative. Industry consultants’ updated forecasts are corroborating what we are seeing from our customers, which is slowing producer activity that likely results in slightly slower Permian natural gas production growth. In-service is expected during the second quarter of 2026. In addition, commercial negotiations continue as the Company works toward finalizing the next stage of a processing capacity expansion at Kings Landing. Under the contract, Kinetik will deliver residue natural gas at a designated interconnect on the Permian Highway Pipeline, ultimately representing approximately 0.5 MTPA. The gas will be priced monthly based on the European TTF index, offering Kinetik producer customers further diversification of natural gas pricing. This agreement underscores Kinetik’s differentiated service offering and its commitment to unique, innovative, and competitive solutions in the Permian Basin. title: Cloud Windows Sandboxes GA + macOS Preview
summary: Announcing general availability of Cloud Windows Sandboxes and preview of macOS Sandboxes on Cua Cloud.
body_text: If you've been building with our cua libraries, you might've hit a limitation with local computer-use sandboxes: to run agents on Windows or macOS, you need to be on that OS - Windows Sandbox for Windows, Apple Virtualization for macOS. The only cross-platform option is Linux on Docker, which limits you to virtualizing Linux environments ( see all local options here ). title: The Future of Substance Use Care Is AI-Native
summary: Why the next generation of healthcare software won't bolt AI onto legacy EHRs. Pelago CEO on building Atlas for substance use care.
body_text: A clinician finishes a 50-minute session. The member leaves. The clinician opens their laptop and begins the second session: 45 minutes of documentation. They reconstruct the conversation from memory, translate it into billing codes, fill templates designed for auditors, and hunt through tabs to cross-reference previous notes. Then they move to the next patient. This happens six times a day. More time documenting than treating. It’s not an edge case. It’s the norm. Show me the incentive and I’ll show you the outcome Electronic Health Records (EHRs) were never built for care. They were built for billing. The systems designed in the 1990s now stand between clinicians and patients, optimized to capture every action, convert it into codes, and generate revenue. Clinical workflows became data-entry workflows – serving payers, not patients. This design misalignment produces predictable distortions. Providers maximize billable sessions because income scales with time spent, not outcomes achieved. The financial incentive isn’t to solve the problem efficiently. It’s to extend the engagement. In that sense, the system isn’t broken, it’s working exactly as intended. The flaw lies in what it was designed to optimize. The consequences are staggering. The U.S. spends roughly $50 billion each year on substance use disorder (SUD) treatment, yet reaches only about 10% of those in need. The remaining 90%, generate an estimated $135 billion in preventable downstream costs, from ER visits to comorbidity complications to inpatient care. We’re spending more and helping fewer. The bottleneck isn’t money. It’s infrastructure built around the wrong objective function. Innovation means reducing cost while expanding access Pelago was founded on the belief that true innovation expands access to care while sharply reducing costs. By reinventing the way addiction care gets delivered through technology, Pelago’s digital clinic has reduced the average cost to treat someone with a SUD from $30,000 in traditional outpatient settings to just $3,000, delivering a 4.5:1 ROI to employers through reduced medical claims. The foundation is a value-based care reimbursement model. Employers and health plans pay a fixed amount per member, not per session. The incentive shifts from billable hours to outcomes, making efficient care profitable, not just possible. That alignment enabled us to build Atlas, Pelago’s AI-native EHR designed from the ground up to maximize clinical impact per hour of clinician time. The platform has three components: context preparation, real-time guidance, and documentation automation. Before the call: smart triaging, full context Atlas continuously analyzes clinical signals, engagement patterns, and contextual data to automatically surface members who may be at risk or in crisis. This smart triaging capability helps care teams prioritize outreach, escalate clinical support when needed, and ensure that the highest-risk members receive timely, personalized attention. Ahead of each session, Atlas generates a clinical summary of the member’s history and recent interactions. The clinician opens the session with full context already assembled: previous concerns, medication changes, family dynamics, recent check-ins. No tab-switching, timeline reconstruction, or spending the first 10 minutes piecing together fragmented notes. The narrative is coherent before the conversation starts. This matters more than it sounds. As a physician, I’ve seen firsthand how coming into a session with context sharpens the conversation. Clinicians ask better questions, pick up on subtle shifts in mood or behavior, and earn trust faster. Preparation creates precision. During the call: evidence in real time During a session, the care co-pilot surfaces evidence-based strategies personalized to the member in real time. When a member mentions sleep disruption, Atlas instantly retrieves trauma-informed techniques relevant to their treatment history. The clinician stays fully engaged in the conversation instead of mentally flipping through protocol manuals. This transforms the balance between presence and rigor. Clinicians no longer have to choose between warmth and thoroughness. Atlas carries the guidelines, the clinician carries the connection, and together, they deliver better care. After the call: documentation done After the call, AI-assisted notes record, transcribe, and summarize the interaction. Documentation completes automatically. The clinician closes their laptop and transitions to the next patient. The 45-minute admin block vanishes. The impact goes beyond incremental efficiency gains. By eliminating a bottleneck that consumed half the working day, Atlas fundamentally changes how clinicians spend their time. How we’re building AI for substance use care Atlas reflects Pelago’s approach to AI: purpose-built for substance use care. In substance use care, the line between helpful and harmful is often invisible to general-purpose systems. An off-the-shelf model trained on the open internet won’t understand the nuances of motivational interviewing or when a member’s statement requires immediate human intervention. Every AI capability at Pelago is grounded in evidence-based practices. The system knows its boundaries and hands off to human care when it reaches them, with full context intact. Member data is protected structurally, from storage to transmission to access. The goal isn’t to automate care but to amplify it by freeing clinicians to focus on connection while strengthening the care every member receives. Building for a new paradigm Atlas represents a bet that the next generation of healthcare software won’t be built by bolting AI onto legacy platforms. The systems designed for fee-for-service billing, with their emphasis on CPT codes, encounter forms, and defensible documentation, carry too much embedded assumption about what matters. Vertically integrating specialty care, with AI as the foundation rather than the add-on, allows different design choices. This matters beyond Pelago. Behavioral health sits at the intersection of two crises: surging need and shrinking capacity. We can’t solve that equation by asking clinicians to work harder within the old system. We need technology that genuinely multiplies clinical impact, not software that tracks the work of care while slowing down the work itself. Atlas works because we control both the technology and the care delivery. The real test is whether employers and health plans are willing to address the misaligned incentives that still dominate most of healthcare. Software alone won’t fix incentive structures. But when the economic model rewards outcomes and the technology stack serves that goal, we get a glimpse of what’s possible: clinicians practicing at the top of their license, members receiving personalized support at scale, and systems learning their way toward better care. The question isn’t whether AI belongs in behavioral health. It’s whether we’ll use it to optimize the old paradigm or build a new one. Read more about Pelago Atlas in our Fall Product Update

title: Signs of Strep Throat & How to Treat It
summary: Recognize the signs of strep throat and prevent complications. Book a virtual visit for rapid evaluation, antibiotic treatment, and care guidance.
body_text: Signs of Strep Throat & How to Treat It What Causes a Sore Throat and When It Might Be Strep A sore throat can signal many things, but when bacteria are to blame, fast treatment matters. When your throat feels raw, you may ask yourself, “Is this strep?” Strep throat, caused by group A Streptococcus bacteria (Streptococcus pyogenes), is one of the most common bacterial infections of the throat. While most sore throats stem from viral illnesses, strep infections require specific antibiotic treatment to prevent serious complications like rheumatic fever or kidney inflammation. Early diagnosis helps you recover faster and reduces the risk of spreading the infection to others. Early care helps ensure a quicker recovery and prevents strep throat from spreading to others. With Circle Medical , you can connect virtually with a licensed primary care doctor who can evaluate your symptoms and determine whether they may be consistent with strep throat. When appropriate, they can make a clinical diagnosis and begin treatment based on your symptoms and history. If confirmation of strep diagnosis is needed, your Circle Medical provider may advise you to go to an in-person location—such as an urgent care clinic—for a rapid strep test or throat culture, which must be done in person. Circle Medical clinicians cannot order rapid strep tests or throat cultures , as commercial labs (Quest, Labcorp) do not collect throat swabs. Strep testing is available during an in-person appointment at select in-person locations, where a clinician can perform a rapid strep test or collect a throat culture if indicated. If you already know you want a definitive test, going directly to urgent care or a nearby clinic may be the most efficient option. How Strep Bacteria Cause Infection and Complications Strep throat is more than a bad sore throat. It’s a contagious bacterial infection that can spread quickly and cause serious complications without timely care. How infection begins: Strep throat starts when group A Streptococcus bacteria enter through the mouth or nose and attach to the lining of the throat and tonsils. These bacteria spread easily through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or when utensils and drinks are shared. Who’s most at risk: Though school-age children are most commonly affected, anyone can get a strep throat infection through close contact or crowded environments like classrooms or offices. Why early care matters: Without antibiotic treatment, the infection can trigger rheumatic fever, kidney inflammation, or, in rare cases, toxic shock syndrome. Early evaluation by a Circle Medical primary care doctor ensures safe, evidence-based care that prevents complications and stops the spread of infection. What Does Strep Throat Look Like? Strep throat has telltale signs like redness, swelling, and white patches. But testing is the only way to know for sure. Feature What Strep Throat Looks Like What It’s Commonly Mistaken For Tonsils Red, inflamed, may show white patches or streaks of pus Mild redness without white patches (viral sore throat) Roof of Mouth Small red spots (petechiae) Usually clear in viral or allergic irritation Neck Area Tender lymph nodes or swollen glands Mild tenderness or none in viral infections Additional Clues Sudden throat pain, fever, fatigue Runny nose, cough, or gradual onset (viral or allergic) Only a rapid strep test or throat culture can confirm a strep infection. These tests must be done in person at a clinic or urgent care, and Circle Medical clinicians cannot order or perform them through virtual appointments. Visual symptoms help raise suspicion, but testing ensures accurate diagnosis and the right treatment. Strep Throat Symptoms You Shouldn’t Ignore Strep throat symptoms can come on fast and hit hard, unlike viral sore throats that creep up slowly. Recognizing these red flags early helps you get the right care and avoid complications. Common Symptoms When a strep throat infection takes hold, symptoms often appear suddenly and feel intense. Here’s what to look for: Severe throat pain that makes swallowing difficult Fever (often around or above 101°F / 38.3°C) Swollen tonsils with redness or white patches Tender lymph nodes in the neck Headache, body aches, or fatigue Nausea or vomiting, particularly in children How Symptoms Differ by Age Even if symptoms seem clear, a rapid strep test or throat culture is the best way to confirm diagnosis, and these tests require an in-person visit rather than a telehealth appointment. Children: Higher fevers, stomach pain, and potential rash (called scarlet fever) Adults: Throat-centered pain, fewer stomach-related symptoms How Strep Throat Spreads, and How to Stop It Strep throat spreads easily through close contact and droplets, but simple steps and timely treatment can stop it in its tracks. How Strep Throat Spreads The bacteria spread through droplets when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks, and can linger on shared items like utensils or toothbrushes. Even brief contact, such as touching a contaminated surface and then your mouth or nose, can pass the infection. How Long You’re Contagious You can pass the infection to others: 2–5 days after exposure , even before symptoms appear Up to 24 hours after starting antibiotics That’s why it’s essential to stay home from work or school until you’ve taken antibiotics for at least a full day and your fever has resolved. Prevention Tips Stopping the spread starts with small, consistent actions: Wash your hands regularly or use alcohol-based hand sanitizer Avoid sharing utensils, drinks, or towels Consider replacing your toothbrush after 24–48 hours on antibiotics as a precaution Cover your mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing With early treatment and good hygiene, you can protect yourself and others from infection. When to Choose Telehealth vs. Urgent Care Circle Medical clinicians can clinically assess symptoms and may diagnose and treat strep throat based on your presentation alone. However, if needed a confirmatory rapid strep test must be done in person at an urgent care or clinic. Circle Medical cannot order or perform throat swabs unless you are booked an in-person appointment at a select in-person location. If you prefer definitive testing, or if you are unsure whether clinical diagnosis alone is right for you, it may be better to go directly to urgent care to avoid a second visit or copay. Strep Throat Diagnosis: Tests and What to Expect Testing is the only reliable way to confirm strep throat, and knowing what to expect can help you feel confident and prepared for your visit. Types of Diagnostic Tests When symptoms suggest a strep throat infection, your provider may recommend one or both of the following tests: Rapid antigen test (rapid strep test): A quick throat swab that detects bacterial proteins in minutes. It’s highly convenient but not always conclusive. Throat culture: A more sensitive test where a sample is grown in a lab to detect group A Streptococcus bacteria. It provides confirmation within 24–48 hours. If your symptoms are strongly suggestive of strep throat, your clinician may make a clinical diagnosis, prescribe antibiotics, and guide your recovery plan, even without a throat swab. If your symptoms are unclear, overlap with viral infections, or you prefer definitive testing, your clinician will recommend that you go to a local urgent care or in-person clinic for a rapid strep test or further evaluation. Because Circle Medical is a telehealth service, our clinicians cannot perform or order rapid strep tests or throat cultures. Urgent care or in-person clinic visits for throat swab testing are separate from your Circle Medical visit and may involve an additional copay or out-of-pocket cost. If you already know you want a strep test to confirm the diagnosis, it may be better to go directly to urgent care instead of starting with a virtual visit. Clinicians at select in-person locations can collect rapid strep tests or throat cultures if an in-person appointment is booked. This approach ensures you receive accurate answers and evidence-based care while understanding when telehealth is appropriate and when in-person testing is the better next step. Treating Strep Throat: Medications, Care, and Recovery Tips With the right antibiotic treatment and supportive care, most people recover from strep throat within a week and start feeling better within just a couple of days. Standard Treatments Antibiotic treatment: A prescribed course of penicillin or amoxicillin is the most common approach. For those with allergies, your clinician may recommend another effective alternative. Symptom relief: Ease discomfort with warm salt-water gargles, throat lozenges, hydration, and plenty of rest. Gentle care like drinking warm liquids or using a cool mist vaporizer can also soothe throat pain. Recovery Timeline 24–48 hours: Most patients notice symptom relief soon after starting antibiotics. 1–2 days: Fever typically subsides as the body responds to treatment. After recovery: Consider replacing your toothbrush after 24–48 hours on antibiotics as a precaution and continue your antibiotic course exactly as prescribed. Following your clinician’s guidance helps ensure a full recovery, prevents complications, and minimizes the risk of spreading infection to others. From virtual visits to prescriptions, every step is designed around your comfort and convenience. Get personalized next steps, including clinical treatment when appropriate or guidance to in-person urgent care for testing and follow-up, based on your symptoms and risk factors. How to Know If Your Strep Throat Needs Urgent Attention Some symptoms mean it’s time to stop waiting and seek in-person medical care right away. Knowing when to act can protect your health and prevent serious complications . Go to the ER or Call 911 If You Experience: Difficulty breathing or swallowing, especially if it worsens quickly Persistent high fever (e.g., ≥102°F / 38.9°C) that doesn’t improve with medication Rash that looks like scaly, teardrop-shaped spots. This is a possible sign of scarlet fever Severe dehydration, confusion, or dark urine, which may indicate kidney involvement or another serious complication If any of these symptoms appear, don’t wait. Seek emergency care immediately. Quick attention can prevent dangerous complications from an untreated or advanced strep throat infection. Common Questions About Strep Throat, Answered We’ve gathered clear, evidence-based answers to the most common questions patients ask about strep throat: from recovery time to prevention. Q1: Can strep throat go away without antibiotics? While some mild infections may improve on their own, untreated strep throat can lead to serious complications such as rheumatic fever or kidney inflammation. It’s always safest to see a health care provider for proper diagnosis and treatment. Q2: Can you get strep throat without tonsils? Yes. Even without tonsils, group A Streptococcus bacteria can still infect the throat and surrounding tissues. Q3: How soon can I return to work or school after starting antibiotics? Most people are no longer contagious 24 hours after starting antibiotics and once they’re fever-free. Always finish the full antibiotic course to ensure recovery and prevent reinfection. Q4: Is strep throat seasonal? Yes. Strep throat cases peak in winter and early spring, when indoor contact makes it easier for strep bacteria to spread. Practicing good hand hygiene helps reduce your risk year-round.
